note: The third topic bank. Covers the material outside FYM and hotel-tech: team/process (PM + lead + dev + designer, onboarding, custom vs template), e-commerce, mobile apps, integrations, general (non-hotel) WordPress work, and Kymbo's operating principles. This is the 'wider positioning' material Isa asked for on 2026-08-11 — carousels that speak about the whole shop, not just the campaign. Verified against Notion 2026-08-03 (see stack.json).

pillars.The Team: Who does what, when, and why the shape works.
pillars.The Process: How a project actually runs, step by step, transparently.
pillars.The Craft: Positions Kymbo takes on how work should be done — with the reason.
pillars.The Range: What Kymbo builds beyond hotels — e-commerce, mobile, integrations, custom.
pillars.The Culture: The nearshore team, timezone reality, how collaboration actually feels.

coverRule: Surface is not fixed — decided per topic. Light covers help the feed's tonal math; dark covers work when the topic has a strong visual anchor (a person, a workspace, a piece of infrastructure).
editorialNote: These carousels are the ones that read as 'brand and craft', not 'sales'. They are the reason a follower who never converts still stays subscribed. Copy discipline is the same as everywhere: no unverified claims, arithmetic > promise, one idea per slide, the 5-year-old test on every sentence.

topics.title: The five people on every Kymbo project
topics.hook: The shape of the team behind your build.
topics.angle: PM, tech lead, developer(s), designer (custom only), client. What each does, when they show up, why the shape works. Anti-'lone freelancer' — Kymbo is a team, not a founder.
proof: PM: client-facing single point of contact
Template projects run without a designer

topics.title: The onboarding week, day by day
topics.hook: From 'yes' to first design in five working days.
topics.angle: Publish the actual onboarding cadence — discovery call, SOW, staging environment, first design pass, first review. Transparency IS the value proposition; nobody else in this market publishes the workflow.
proof: Day 4-5: first design or content pass
End of week: review + revision list

topics.title: Custom or template — how Kymbo picks
topics.hook: You don't need custom. Until you do.
topics.angle: The real decision Kymbo runs, replacing the retired widget/full-integration framing. Template when: content-first site, marketing site, standard flow; custom when: design is a value driver, integrations are non-trivial, performance is load-bearing. Named tradeoffs, not marketing.
proof: custom: capped at 15 active plugins (custom theme)

topics.title: The whole guest lifecycle, not just the booking
topics.hook: Direct isn't a checkout. It's the whole stay.
topics.angle: The C7/C10/C11 fix combined. A direct-booking build handles pre-arrival messaging, door codes, self check-in instructions, staff notifications on check-in/out, in-stay FAQs, post-stay follow-up. This is what closes Airbnb's operational advantage — not just the booking, the automation.
proof: arrival: door code + self check-in instructions
the layer OTAs never gave you: the CRM
topics.source: Notion → Hospitality management + FYM brief; C7/C10/C11 feedback

topics.title: Discovery, SOW, kickoff — the three docs every project starts with
topics.hook: A quote isn't a scope. Here's what actually comes first.
topics.angle: What each document is for, what belongs in it, what does not. Discovery = questions and risks. SOW = named deliverables + timeline + price. Kickoff = who owns what, sign-offs, communication cadence. Publishing this makes Kymbo look like the adult in the room.
proof: kickoff: comms cadence, sign-off owners, staging URL

topics.title: Staging environment, always
topics.hook: The first real booking is the worst place to find the bug.
topics.angle: Every Kymbo build lives on staging before it lives on production. Client-tested, payment-flow-tested, PMS-sync-tested. The client signs off on staging before the domain gets pointed. This is what prevents launch-day disaster stories — publish it, don't hide it.
proof: staging = real dev-staging-prod pipeline (Railway or Cloudflare)
PMS sync tested before go-live (prevents double-booking)
client sign-off gates the domain pointing
topics.source: Notion → campaign brief § Offer (Growth tier); edu-30

topics.title: Why Kymbo doesn't lock clients in
topics.hook: You can take your site elsewhere on day one.
topics.angle: Kymbo hands over: full admin, hosting credentials, backup restore drill, documentation. Competes on ongoing value, not on lock-in. A slightly spicy position because most agencies do the opposite — that's exactly why it converts.
proof: handoff includes admin, hosting, backups, docs
no proprietary CMS, no locked-down theme framework
care plan is opt-in, not required

topics.title: Nearshore, in one timezone
topics.hook: Colombian team. US LLC. Same coffee break.
topics.angle: The genuine argument for nearshore vs offshore: same business hours as US/Canada clients, same-day iteration, no 12-hour handoff cycles. Not a claim about culture — a claim about the clock.
proof: same working hours as US East / Central

topics.title: E-commerce isn't just a Shopify install
topics.hook: You didn't buy a store. You bought a pipeline.
topics.angle: The parts of an e-commerce build that aren't 'add the theme': payment gateway + processor + merchant account (three companies, three fees), tax and shipping logic, inventory sync, abandoned cart, post-purchase email, GA4 events. Kymbo does the pipeline; the theme is 5% of the work.
proof: shipping: real-time rates or flat, per SKU
post-purchase: order confirmation + shipping + review request

topics.title: When mobile is the right answer (and when it isn't)
topics.hook: A mobile app is a commitment, not a feature.
topics.angle: The honest decision Kymbo runs before quoting a mobile build. Yes when: repeat-use, offline capability, native device features (camera, push, geofence), long-term relationship with the same user. No when: content browsing, one-time transaction, would work as a fast responsive site. The 'don't build the app' answer is often the right one.
proof: yes: repeat use, offline, push, native features
no: content browsing, one-time transaction, first-time users
cost signal: mobile ships in 2 stores, updates cost 2x web

topics.title: Every integration is two things: an API and an agreement
topics.hook: APIs never break the way people expect them to.
topics.angle: What makes integrations expensive isn't the code — it's the auth flow, the rate limits, the retry policy, the failure surface (which side rolls back?), and the change contract (who tells whom when the API updates). Kymbo has scars from all five.
proof: auth: OAuth vs API key vs signed JWT — different failure surfaces
rate limits: retry with backoff, not a tight loop
failure: exactly-once is a myth; design for at-least-once
change: version pinning, contract tests, changelogs monitored

topics.title: The check-in flow, automated end-to-end
topics.hook: Guest lands. Door opens. No front desk required.
topics.angle: Concrete companion to craft-04. A single scene walkthrough of what a fully-automated arrival looks like on a Kymbo direct-booking build: SMS/email confirmation with door code, in-app or SMS 'you're here' welcome, self check-in instructions, staff notified only if something fails. Ties the whole 'direct booking > Airbnb operations' argument to a physical moment.
proof: arrival: 'you're here' welcome + wifi + house rules
check-in: no front desk required for standard stays
exception path: staff notified only if guest reports an issue

topics.title: Why performance is a gate, not a feature
topics.angle: Publish the internal performance gate again, this time not as an educational post but as a *position*: some things are non-negotiable. LCP < 2.5s or the build doesn't go live. Explains what changes when performance is treated as a gate versus an aspiration.
topics.source: Notion → WordPress Performance and Core Web Vitals

topics.title: The three things that end up on the review call
topics.hook: Design. Copy. Performance. That's the review.
topics.angle: Transparency about how a Kymbo review actually goes: not 'what do you think of the design' — 'here's the design, here's the copy, here's the performance, sign off on each independently'. Isolates the feedback so it doesn't blur.
proof: design: sign off before content pass
copy: sign off before performance pass

topics.title: Handoff, not lock-in
topics.hook: On go-live day, you get everything.
topics.angle: Companion to craft-07. The handoff checklist Kymbo runs on every project: admin credentials, hosting access, backups verified, documentation, restore drill run. The client leaves the launch call with everything they need to take the site to another agency if they want to. That is Kymbo's competitive posture, not a courtesy.
proof: backup restore drill (actually run, not just documented)
